original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: For the complete five-source, 31-mask batch with pairwise-distinct output maps, does admitting one length-16 connector that is explicitly zeroed and fully charged let per-mask source rebuilding lower the pinned 10-B/64-A dirty-connector schedule?
scope_change_reason: The first refined common-map broadcast scope was already covered by the stronger charged common-A construction in open PR #1707. This changed scope retains distinct output maps and changes the connector contract by admitting exactly one fresh row whose initialization, hosting, scheduler controls, allocation, and release are charged.
bottleneck_link: This tests whether a paid extra connector can exchange source-side work for fewer expensive output-map updates at the recursive interface. The result is a root tariff comparison only and does not establish a new supplier or kappa.
stop_rule: Fix L=16, five cyclic-permutation source maps, 31 affine-permutation output maps, and the declared per-update/per-descriptor tariff. Stop after exact basis replay, four mutation controls, and the complete comparison with the pinned direct schedule; do not expand to other dimensions or tariffs in this cycle.
evidence: python3 -B research/clean-connector-per-mask-seede54e/verify.py passes all 608 F2 bit-column checks, four construction controls, and nine invoice undercharge controls. It verifies pairwise-distinct output maps, the pinned 10-B/64-A comparator, and the complete scalar bill: 41,138 direct versus 38,656 with a fresh row, a 2,482-unit local saving. No kappa or recursive integration is claimed.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: OpenAI Codex provided substantial assistance with the construction analysis, cost derivation, verifier implementation, and package preparation.

open_questions.question: Does the fresh-row source-rebuild schedule remain cheaper after nested composition, child restoration, frame changes, and per-level scheduling are charged?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The current 2,482-unit reduction is only a root comparison; recursive overhead may consume it before it changes a supplier moment or kappa.
open_questions.first_step: Choose one concrete recursive supplier whose source and output map costs match the fixture, then write and evaluate its complete recurrence including hosted rows and every reverse child.
open_questions.blocked_by: No compatible supplier implementation or recursive cost profile is currently bound to this synthetic length-16 map family.
